effort: Apply early braking and purposeful exits across new, fully planned multidirectional routes.
brief: E2 is the final application task: an M-shaped route with three known corners. A gathered stop-to-diagonal restart, compass route, three-hop pattern, crossover-to-backward transition and single-leg push to a shared landing sample complementary force-control demands. This is a new application, not a repeated pre/post test.
marker: For E2, record each of the three corners separately: early braking, controlled foot/knee/pelvis position and two exit steps toward the next target. Report valid corners and routes by mirrored direction; never compare its time directly with another drill's time.
readiness: Review all available actual attendance, loading and response records before delivery. None is currently supplied. Keep the route entry intent conservative; link three hops only at a spacing the athlete can control. Do not use the final class as a maximum test or a reason to finish poor-quality work.
space: The M course and compass exits require a measured 9 m × 7 m clear bay, including abort and stopping corridors. This is the widest requirement in the sequence and is not confirmed by three 10 m lanes. Measure it before delivery; if unavailable, the coach must adapt/defer those drills and record the uncompleted directional coverage rather than imply all twelve were delivered.

drills.name: Gathered Stop-to-Diagonal Restart
drills.execution: Run 1.5 m, brake over 1 m while taking two controlled reorienting steps into a staggered base, hold 1 s, then accelerate 1.5 m along the known 45-degree exit and stop over 2.5 m. No sliding hockey stop.
drills.job: Rebuild a usable base before the next exit when an immediate single-plant cut is unsuitable.
drills.layout: Mark the entry/braking strip and separate diagonal exit/stop. Feet unload before turning; clear a straight abort path beyond the braking strip.
drills.difference: A reoriented two-step gather and deliberate pause precede a diagonal restart; earlier stop-restarts stayed straight and earlier diagonal cuts had no static reset.
drills.regress: Lower entry speed and shorten reorientation steps if the athlete twists over a fixed foot.
drills.exposure: 1 travel redirection and 2 braking episodes; the 1 m initial braking strip is included in path distance.

drills.name: M-Drill Multidirectional Cut — compact course
drills.execution: Run the four marked legs of the M route with controlled braking at its three intermediate cones, then stop over 2 m on the last heading. No cone touching or extra return.
drills.job: Main integration: prepare each next plant while producing an effective exit from the current one.
drills.layout: Local metre coordinates: A(0,0), B(1,1.5), C(2,0.5), D(3,1.5), E(4,0). Legs total about 6.43 m. Translate the pattern into the bay with margins; final stop extends 2 m beyond E along D→E. Mirror across the long axis for the second route; keep tangent abort paths empty.
drills.difference: Four legs and three alternating corner demands, unlike the shorter W/Z/X patterns; the middle valley requires a second reorganization before the last peak.
drills.regress: Reduce speed over all legs if any later corner becomes a rushed pivot; do not add a faster retry.
drills.exposure: 3 cuts and 4 braking episodes per course. Corners are approximately 101, 90 and 101 degrees, not mislabeled as three identical 45-degree cuts.

drills.name: Five-Cone Compass Route — known three-arm sequence
drills.execution: From the centre, run 1 m north, return to centre, run 1 m east, return to centre, then run 1 m south and stop over 1.5 m. All directions are known; west cone marks unused space, not a reaction target.
drills.job: Choose the next force direction at a shared junction after two different returns.
drills.layout: Four outer cones sit 1 m from centre. Travel totals 5 m plus the southward 1.5 m stop. Coach declares a right-foot turn at N and left-foot turn at E; observe actual feet rather than assuming them. Keep centre crossing and all abort paths empty.
drills.difference: Repeated returns to a shared centre with different outgoing arms; unlike a perimeter course or the two-arm V junction.
drills.regress: Lower speed returning to centre if the next arm cannot be entered without an extra gathering hop.
drills.exposure: 4 cuts at N, centre, E and centre, plus 1 terminal stop: 5 braking episodes. Both lateral plant directions occur within the course.

drills.name: Three-Hop Directional Pattern — same leg
drills.execution: On one leg, hop forward 0.2 m, sideways away from the free leg 0.2 m, then diagonally back toward the starting point; hold the third landing 2 s. Mirror on the other leg.
drills.job: Accept and redirect small forces repeatedly while one leg remains the support.
drills.layout: Three close floor targets in a 3 m × 3 m clear area; no height target, no fourth hop. Final diagonal is about 0.28 m, not 0.2 m.
drills.difference: Three same-leg contacts across three vectors; previous linked bounds alternated legs and ended after two flights.
drills.regress: Shrink the target triangle while keeping its sequence; stop if the first/second landing needs free-foot assistance or a setup hop.
drills.exposure: 3 unilateral landings per leg; do not add these to the discrete running-cut count.

drills.name: Crossover Run to Backpedal Exit
drills.execution: Crossover-run laterally 1 m, brake and reorganize into a 1.5 m backward exit relative to the original torso facing; stop over 1.5 m. No spin into a forward sprint.
drills.job: Produce backward force after a crossing lateral entry with the feet untangled.
drills.layout: Use a short L inside the bay; the backward exit and stop run along its long dimension, with 2 m beyond the incoming corner clear.
drills.difference: Crossing-gait entry into backpedal rather than the earlier square shuffle entry or forward-running entry.
drills.regress: Slow the crossover and shorten steps if the athlete cannot find the backward gait without crossing heels.

drills.name: Single-Leg Lateral Push Jump to Two-Foot Landing
drills.execution: Hold a shallow single-leg stance for 1 s, push laterally within 0.3 m and land on both feet for a 2 s hold.
drills.job: Express each plant leg's lateral force while sharing the receiving load at the end of the session.
drills.layout: Clear a 3 m × 3 m landing area; mirror takeoff legs and directions. The free foot joins only for landing.
drills.difference: Unilateral paused takeoff to a bilateral landing; earlier lateral tasks used same-leg/opposite-leg landings or bilateral takeoff.
drills.regress: Shorten flight if the free leg must touch down before takeoff or the shared landing is uncontrolled.
drills.exposure: 1 unilateral takeoff and 1 bilateral landing per attempt.

light.job: Maintain controlled pelvis orientation over each plant leg in the integrated routes.
Maintain active foot pressure across changing exit directions.

strength.job: Maintain shared knee/hip braking capacity after the integrated routes.
Retain hip-hinge force with the familiar technical reserve.
Maintain frontal acceptance and redirected push strength.
Maintain hip extension for short running exits without adding a new lift.
Maintain adductor/pelvis support after multiaxial plants.
Maintain bent-knee ankle force at a low working volume.

previous_review: Class 11 prescribed eight discrete cuts, two bilateral/four unilateral landings and eight primary bouts. No actual athlete observations or performance gains are recorded.
progression: Apply a new known route rather than repeat a test drill. E2 has only two complete courses; supporting compass work is one course. Fourteen discrete changes and eight flight landings are separated in the ledger. This is conditional application, not an earned increase or maximal end test.
strength_progression: Retain the exact Class 11 six-lift selections, single-round doses and technical effort targets. Any smallest-available load adjustment requires actual prior success and recovery; absent those, calibrate conservatively and hold the prescription.
audit: Checked M-route corner angles and path lengths, counted only four compass cuts and kept its order fully known. Separated the three-hop flight contacts from running cuts and used a shared landing in E6 to avoid another unilateral receiving task. Full-sequence review must reconcile all state and historical repeated-drill handoffs. Final arithmetic review rounded the exact M-path length of 6.43398 m to 6.43 m and regenerated its totals.
next: All twelve full prescriptions are now written. Audit the full sequence, saved links, exact counts, mechanical drill distinctions, workload arithmetic and unresolved delivery/athlete assumptions; no Class 13 or claimed athlete improvement.

light_entries.name: Hip Airplane — supported
light_entries.execution: Bodyweight, hand support and slight hip hinge. Slowly open/close pelvis through a small owned arc without rolling the stance foot.
light_entries.rest: Keep easy; rest 30 s between legs.
light_entries.regress: Reduce arc or use more hand support if knee/foot rotates uncontrollably.
light_entries.job: Maintain controlled pelvis orientation over each plant leg in the integrated routes.

light_entries.name: Short-Foot Drill — supported standing hold
light_entries.execution: **5 s relaxed reset** between holds, **30 s between feet**, **60 s before P1**. Stand with most weight on the working foot and fingertip support.
light_entries.regress: Strengthen active arch control while maintaining heel, big-toe base and little-toe base contact for planting. Keep toes long; do not roll onto the outside edge. Use bilateral weight support instead if arch control needs toe-clawing or ankle rolling.
light_entries.job: Maintain active foot pressure across changing exit directions.

strength_entries.name: Goblet Squat
strength_entries.execution: Dumbbell held close; lower 3 s through owned range and stand decisively with both feet grounded.
strength_entries.regress: Reduce load/depth if the trunk folds or heels lift.
strength_entries.job: Maintain shared knee/hip braking capacity after the integrated routes.

strength_entries.name: Romanian Deadlift — two dumbbells
strength_entries.execution: bilateral; **2 s down**, purposeful hip extension; 2–3 RIR. Rest **120 s between working sets**.
strength_entries.regress: Maintain a softly bent, nearly constant knee angle, weights close and a controlled back position; stop lowering at the owned range.
strength_entries.job: Retain hip-hinge force with the familiar technical reserve.

strength_entries.name: Lateral Lunge — goblet dumbbell
strength_entries.execution: step out, lower **2 s**, push back to the original stance; 2–3 RIR. Rest **60 s between legs**.
strength_entries.regress: Keep the lunging foot grounded and knee aligned; sit into that hip without rotating away. Reduce width, depth or load for loss of control.
strength_entries.job: Maintain frontal acceptance and redirected push strength.

strength_entries.name: Hip Thrust — dumbbell
strength_entries.execution: Upper back on a stable bench, dumbbell secured over pelvis; rise to hip extension without arching the back, lower 2 s.
strength_entries.regress: Reduce load/range for lumbar extension or hamstring cramp.
strength_entries.alternative: If bench geometry is unsuitable, use instead a loaded dynamic floor glute bridge at the same rep/effort and preparation dose.
strength_entries.job: Maintain hip extension for short running exits without adding a new lift.

strength_entries.name: Copenhagen Side Plank — short lever
strength_entries.execution: top knee/lower thigh on a stable bench, lower leg clear. Rest **60 s between sides**. Use bodyweight; if already controlled and too easy, secure a small dumbbell at the upper hip with the upper hand to reach the holding-effort target.
strength_entries.regress: Keep shoulder comfortable and pelvis level. Use light lower-foot assistance if needed; stop for groin/shoulder pain or loss of position.
strength_entries.alternative: If no suitable stable Copenhagen support fits, use instead floor side-lying hip adduction, upper foot on the floor in front, 1 × 8 per lower leg at 2–3 RIR with 60 s between sides; add a small hand-secured dumbbell above the inner knee only if needed and comfortable. Its preparation is 1 × 4 easy reps per leg instead of the hold ramps. This proposed replacement adds 16 dynamic working reps and removes 30 s of working holds; preparation adds 8 reps and removes 10 s of holds. Bouts are unchanged; allow up to 2 extra minutes.
strength_entries.job: Maintain adductor/pelvis support after multiaxial plants.

strength_entries.name: Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated, dumbbells on thighs
strength_entries.execution: bilateral; knees near 90°, forefeet on floor, **1 s at top, 2 s lowering, quiet bottom reset**; 2–3 RIR. Rest **90 s between sets**.
strength_entries.regress: Secure the weights above the knees, maintain knee angle and repeatable heel rise. Reduce load if heel height falls or bouncing replaces muscle force.
strength_entries.alternative: For seated calf work, use a securely held sandbag instead of dumbbells when its shape and load fit better.
strength_entries.job: Maintain bent-knee ankle force at a low working volume.
